arxiv-1401-4685.title: Perturbative large deviation analysis of non-equilibrium dynamics
arxiv-1401-4685.creator: Gino Del Ferraro, Erik Aurell
arxiv-1401-4685.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by Gino Del Ferraro, Erik Aurell. Macroscopic fluctuation theory has shown that a wide class of non-equilibrium stochastic dynamical systems obey a large deviation principle, but except for a few one-dimensional examples these large deviation principles are in general not known in closed form. We consider the problem of constructing successive approximations to an (unknown) large deviation functional and show that the non-equilibrium probability distribution the takes a Gibbs-Boltzmann form with a set of auxiliary (non-physical) energy functions.

arxiv-2105-14581.title: Simulating of X-states and the two-qubit XYZ Heisenberg system on IBM quantum computer
arxiv-2105-14581.creator: Fereshte Shahbeigi, Mahsa Karimi, Vahid Karimipour
arxiv-2105-14581.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Fereshte Shahbeigi, Mahsa Karimi, Vahid Karimipour. Two qubit density matrices which are of X-shape, are a natural generalization of Bell Diagonal States (BDSs) recently simulated on the IBM quantum device. We generalize the previous results and propose a quantum circuit for simulation of a general two qubit X-state, implement it on the same quantum device, and study its entanglement for several values of the extended parameter space. We also show that their X-shape is approximately robust against noisy quantum gates.

arxiv-2501-17580.title: Field-induced upward bending of a magnetoelastomer cantilever residing on a horizontal plane: an unconventional cilium
arxiv-2501-17580.creator: O. V. Stolbov, G. V. Stepanov, Yu. L. Raikher
arxiv-2501-17580.description: Abstract The mechanical response of a cantilever made of a magnetoactive elastomer (MAE) that is positioned on a solid plane surface and is subjected to a uniform magnetic field is studied. The MAE is of the magnetically soft type, i.e., its filler particles become magnetized only in the presence of external field.

arxiv-2505-16781.title: Fuzzy Information Evolution with Three-Way Decision in Social Network Group Decision-Making
arxiv-2505-16781.creator: Qianlei Jia, Xinliang Zhou, Ondrej Krejcar, Enrique Herrera-Viedma (Fellow, IEEE)
arxiv-2505-16781.description: Abstract In group decision-making (GDM) scenarios, uncertainty, dynamic social structures, and vague information present major challenges for traditional opinion dynamics models. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel social network group decision-making (SNGDM) framework that integrates three-way decision (3WD) theory, dynamic network reconstruction, and linguistic opinion representation.

arxiv-2506-19255.title: From Data Acquisition to Lag Modeling: Quantitative Exploration of A-Share Market with Low-Coupling System Design
arxiv-2506-19255.creator: Fang Jianyong
arxiv-2506-19255.description: Abstract This paper presents a comprehensive two-stage approach to detect and analyze lead-lag effects in the Chinese A-share market. Our methodology first identifies highly coupled stock pairs through long-term data analysis, then verifies the presence of lead-lag relationships using high-frequency data.

arxiv-2507-00216.title: Towards Style Alignment in Cross-Cultural Translation
arxiv-2507-00216.creator: Shreya Havaldar, Adam Stein, Eric Wong, & Lyle UngarUniversity of Pennsylvania {shreyah,steinad,exwong,ungar}@seas.upenn.edu
arxiv-2507-00216.description: Abstract Successful communication depends on the speaker’s intended style (i.e., what the speaker is trying to convey) aligning with the listener’s interpreted style (i.e., what the listener perceives). However, cultural differences often lead to misalignment between the two; for example, politeness is often lost in translation.

arxiv-2508-07571.title: Towards Theoretical Understanding of Transformer Test-Time Computing: Investigation on In-Context Linear Regression
arxiv-2508-07571.creator: Xingwu Chen, Miao Lu, Beining Wu, Difan Zou
arxiv-2508-07571.description: Abstract Using more test-time computation during language model inference, such as generating more intermediate thoughts or sampling multiple candidate answers, has proven effective in significantly improving model performance. This paper takes an initial step toward bridging the gap between practical language model inference and theoretical transformer analysis by incorporating randomness and sampling.

arxiv-2512-08535.title: Photo3D: Advancing Photorealistic 3D Generation through Structure‑Aligned Detail Enhancement https://liangsanzhu.github.io/photo3d-page/
arxiv-2512-08535.creator: Xinyue Liang, Zhiyuan Ma, Lingchen Sun, Yanjun Guo, Lei Zhang
arxiv-2512-08535.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xinyue Liang, Zhiyuan Ma, Lingchen Sun, Yanjun Guo, Lei Zhang. Although recent 3D‑native generators have made great progress in synthesizing reliable geometry, they still fall short in achieving realistic appearances. A key obstacle lies in the lack of diverse and high-quality real-world 3D assets with rich texture details, since capturing such data is intrinsically difficult due to the diverse scales of scenes, non‑rigid motions of objects, and the limited precision of 3D scanners.

arxiv-2601-02097.title: Prospects for identifying pulsar candidates in radio surveys using scintillation
arxiv-2601-02097.creator: Jitendra Salal, Shriharsh P. Tendulkar, Visweshwar Ram Marthi
arxiv-2601-02097.description: Abstract In our previous paper, we developed a technique for identifying pulsar candidates in interferometric radio images using their distinctive scintillation signatures. Building on this technique, the present study simulates a pulsar population using the PsrPopPy Python module to investigate the technique’s limitations and detection capabilities.

pmc-10734425.title: Clostridium butyricum and Clostridium tyrobutyricum: angel or devil for necrotizing enterocolitis?
pmc-10734425.creator: Ruizhi Tao, Gangfan Zong, Yehua Pan, Hongxing Li, Peng Cheng, Rui Deng, Wenxing Chen, Aiyun Wang, Shishan Xia, Weibing Tang, Yin Lu, Zhonghong Wei
pmc-10734425.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a challenging gastrointestinal disease that disproportionately affects premature neonates, with high incidence and case-fatality rates. Despite extensive research efforts, the pathogenesis and mechanisms of NEC remain unclear, making it difficult to effectively eradicate. However, it has been established that dysbiosis of gut microbes occurs before the onset of NEC, providing compelling evidence for the potential use of probiotic therapy.

pmc-12387164.title: Comparison of Pulsed Radiofrequency and Endoscopic Piriformis Release for Refractory Piriformis Syndrome: A Propensity Score-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-12387164.creator: Eunsung Park, Duyoung Choi, Cheol Lee, Cyrus Motamed
pmc-12387164.description: Background/Objective: Piriformis syndrome (PS) causes sciatic nerve entrapment and chronic pain. In refractory cases, pulsed radiofrequency (PRF) and endoscopic piriformis release (EPR) are used, but comparative evidence is limited. Methods: This retrospective cohort study compared PRF and EPR in patients treated from 2018 to 2024 at a tertiary hospital using propensity score matching (PSM).

pmc-12750775.title: First-trimester atherogenic index of plasma and triglyceride–glucose indices in pregestational diabetes mellitus: associations with adverse pregnancy outcomes
pmc-12750775.creator: Serenat Eris Yalcin, Nuray Nerez, Yakup Yalcin, Bilge Demir Cetinkaya
pmc-12750775.description: BackgroundPregestational diabetes mellitus (PREGDM) confers a high risk of maternal and perinatal morbidity. Identifying early, reliable biomarkers is critical for risk stratification. The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) and triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index are inexpensive metabolic markers reflecting dyslipidemia and insulin resistance, but their role in PREGDM remains underexplored.

pmc-13382311.title: Characterization of Angle-Angle Diameter Relationship with Corneal Diameter, Axial Length, and Intraocular Pressure in Pediatric Glaucoma
pmc-13382311.creator: Taylor Kolosky, Reshmi Talwar, He Eun Forbes, Andrew Lee, Moran R Levin, Janet L Alexander
pmc-13382311.description: ObjectiveTo characterize the relationship of angle-angle diameter (AA) with intraocular pressure (IOP), corneal diameter (CD), and axial length (AL) in pediatric patients with glaucoma.DesignProspective cross-sectional observational study.ParticipantsNineteen participants (34 eyes) aged 0.12 to 12.5 years (median = 1.5 years) with pediatric glaucoma.MethodsUltrasound biomicroscopy (UBM), A-scan biometry, and IOP and CD measurement were performed under general anesthesia prior to intraocular surgery.

pmc-13495585.title: Is it time to make brain health a vital sign?
pmc-13495585.creator: Gregory Cooper
pmc-13495585.description: Additionally, these therapies are only indicated for patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to Alzheimer’s Disease or mild Alzheimer’s Disease, leaving many patients ineligible. While research continues to explore various other pharmacologic strategies for the treatment of dementia, the role of lifestyle has begun to emerge.

pmc-13537528.title: DNAmBERT: a transformer-based model for non-invasive cancer diagnosis using DNA sequence and methylation data
pmc-13537528.creator: Maryam Yassi, Mark Ezegbogu, Euan J Rodger, Peter Stockwell, Aniruddha Chatterjee, Matthew Parry
pmc-13537528.description: DNA methylation alterations are early and stable hallmarks of cancer and represent promising biomarkers for non-invasive detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). However, current computational approaches often model DNA sequence and methylation features separately and struggle to capture complex read-level methylation architecture in heterogeneous, low-signal liquid biopsy data.

pmc-13595186.title: Wastewater-Based Surveillance of Human Papillomavirus Genotype Diversity
pmc-13595186.creator: Pauline Michon, Nicolas Cluzel, Yvon Maday, Jean-Luc Prétet, Sabrina Guérin, Rose Lecat, Thomas Thiébault, Vincent Maréchal
pmc-13595186.description: Key PointsQuestionCan wastewater-based epidemiology monitor population-level circulation of human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes?FindingsIn this 1-year cross-sectional study of wastewater from the Paris, France, metropolitan area, 27 HPV genotypes were detected, with a median of 6 genotypes per sample. HPV-66, HPV-6, and HPV-53 were the most frequently detected genotypes, whereas HPV-16 and HPV-18 were detected less often.
